findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation uses os.path.basename to strip traversal paths, but it does not prevent all possible path traversal attacks. A more robust approach is to validate the filename against a whitelist or use a library like pathlib to handle path manipulation. This ensures that only authorized files can be accessed, preventing potential security vulnerabilities.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks by using a whitelist approach or a library like pathlib
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename or '..' in filename or '/' in filename or '\' in filename: return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. To fix this, the enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter should be set to enable logging for error, general, and slowquery logs. This will allow CloudWatch to collect and store logs for the DB instance.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.title: EC2 instance has public IP
findings.description: The EC2 instance has a public IP assigned, which poses a security risk as it can be accessed from the internet. To fix this, set associate_public_ip_address to false, ensuring the instance is only accessible within the VPC. This change prevents direct internet access to the instance.
findings.fix_hint: Remove the public IP assignment from the EC2 instance resource

findings.title: S3 access logging disabled
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_18 check failed because the S3 bucket resource 'aws_s3_bucket.app_data' does not have access logging enabled, which is a security best practice to monitor and track access to the bucket. To fix this, the logging configuration needs to be set on the S3 bucket resource. This can be done by adding a 'logging' block to the 'aws_s3_bucket' resource with the target bucket and prefix specified.
findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 access logging by setting the logging configuration on the S3 bucket resource

findings.title: S3 versioning disabled
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_21 check failed because S3 versioning is disabled, which can lead to data loss in case of accidental deletion or overwrite. Enabling versioning allows for the storage of multiple versions of an object, enabling recovery of previous versions. This can be achieved by adding the versioning block to the aws_s3_bucket resource in the Terraform configuration.
findings.fix_hint: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket to track changes and prevent data loss

findings.title: Ckv Aws 161
findings.description: The CKV_AWS_161 check failed because the AWS DB instance 'app_db' does not have deletion protection enabled, which could lead to accidental deletion of the database. Enabling deletion protection prevents the database from being deleted, even if the Terraform configuration is modified to delete it. This can be achieved by adding the 'deletion_protection' argument to the 'aws_db_instance' resource and setting it to 'true'
findings.fix_hint: Enable deletion protection for the AWS DB instance to prevent accidental deletion

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: ec2:*
findings.description: The current policy allows full EC2 control, which is a security risk. To fix this, the ec2 actions should be restricted to only those necessary for the application. For example, if the application only needs to describe instances, the policy should be updated to only include the ec2:DescribeInstances action.
findings.fix_hint: Remove or restrict the overly permissive ec2 actions in the policy

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: s3:*
findings.description: The original policy grants full S3 access on all buckets due to the wildcard action 's3:*' not being present but 's3:GetObject' and 's3:PutObject' are specified which is still a broad permission. The fixed code restricts S3 actions to 's3:GetObject' and 's3:PutObject' on the 'my-app-data' bucket. This change reduces the attack surface by limiting S3 access to a specific bucket.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict S3 actions to specific resources and remove wildcard permissions

attack_chains.title: EC2 Public IP and Unrestricted SSH
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain initial access to the EC2 instance using the public IP and then exploit the unrestricted SSH access to gain full control of the instance. This allows them to exfiltrate sensitive data and escalate privileges. The attacker can then use the instance as a pivot point to attack other resources in the cloud environment.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains initial access to the EC2 instance using the public IP (finding 25e9676c in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
Step 2: attacker exploits the unrestricted SSH access (finding d398ca72 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf) to gain full control of the instance
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group to only allow access from trusted IP addresses

attack_chains.title: Path Traversal and S3 Access
attack_chains.description: An attacker can use the path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive data on the instance and then use the S3 access to exfiltrate the data. The attacker can then use the exfiltrated data to escalate privileges and gain full control of the cloud environment.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses the path traversal vulnerability (finding 06d4a43a in file src/app.py) to access sensitive data on the instance
Step 2: attacker uses the S3 access (finding ba8df73b in file iam/policy.json) to exfiltrate the sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Fix the path traversal vulnerability by updating the code to properly validate user input

attack_chains.title: EC2 Instance and IAM Privileges
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain initial access to the EC2 instance and then use the IAM privileges to escalate their access and gain full control of the cloud environment. The attacker can then use the instance as a pivot point to attack other resources in the cloud environment.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains initial access to the EC2 instance using the public IP (finding 25e9676c in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
Step 2: attacker uses the IAM privileges (finding a244bc0a in file iam/policy.json) to escalate their access and gain full control of the cloud environment
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict IAM privileges to only allow necessary access to the EC2 instance
